agent_scope: additional distinct-game proofs for methods that had fewer than two; reuses already-registered sources, declares gaps where no shipped evidence exists

sources.title: Portal 2 (Wikipedia)
sources.locator: Game article: release, developer, engine and portal gameplay sections
sources.applicability_note: Secondary encyclopedic source used only to establish that the shipped title exists and is built around recursive portal rendering. Not used for any performance figure.

game_examples.fact: The world is persisted per region/chunk rather than as one monolithic save file, so saving an arbitrarily large world only rewrites the regions that actually changed.
game_examples.locator: Chunk format / region file layout
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example of incremental, region-granular persistence: the save cost scales with what changed, not with world size.
game_examples.non_transferable: Minecraft's chunk format is a bespoke, simple record layout. It does not model Unity/Unreal serialized objects, and its write amplification behaviour will not match a GameObject or UObject save graph.

game_examples.fact: A procedurally generated universe is persisted as the player modifies it, so the save cannot be a full snapshot of generated content and must record only player-made deltas.
game_examples.locator: Continuous World Generation talk: persistence of procedural content
game_examples.relevance: Shows the extreme case that forces incremental saving: content too large to ever write out in full, so only deltas can be stored.
game_examples.non_transferable: No Man's Sky's delta format is tied to its deterministic generation seeds; a project without deterministic regeneration cannot copy this approach.

game_examples.fact: A fast multiplayer shooter with many simultaneous positional sound sources plus voice chat, so the audio system must stream and mix under a fixed memory and latency budget.
game_examples.locator: 'Overwatch' Gameplay Architecture and Netcode (GDC): audio/voice handling
game_examples.relevance: Demonstrates the constraint that makes audio streaming a budget item rather than a convenience: many concurrent emitters under a hard frame budget.
game_examples.non_transferable: The source describes architecture, not codec settings; no bitrate or CPU figure is published, so no numeric audio budget can be derived from it.

game_examples.fact: A shipped open-city title with a very large and heterogeneous material set, and a later path-traced mode that stresses shader variety across the whole scene.
game_examples.locator: Path Tracing & Overdrive Mode - requirements and implementation notes
game_examples.relevance: Provides the scale condition under which bindless resources and uber-shader consolidation become worth their complexity: material count and shader permutation count.
game_examples.non_transferable: REDengine 4 is a bespoke engine; its material system and permutation strategy are not transferable, and this source does not state that bindless binding is used.

game_examples.fact: Soft-body vehicle simulation in which each vehicle is a mass-spring network producing many interacting bodies, so broadphase cost is driven by deformable-node count rather than by vehicle count alone.
game_examples.locator: Soft-body Physics - BeamNG.drive (GDC/technical presentation)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped case where the broadphase input is an order of magnitude larger than the visible object count, which is exactly the condition broadphase partitioning addresses.
game_examples.non_transferable: BeamNG is a simulation-first title running on desktop CPUs; its body counts and solver settings do not represent an action game's physics load.

game_examples.fact: A fully destructible voxel world in which destroying a structure turns one object into a very large number of bodies, so the broadphase must absorb a sudden, localised spike.
game_examples.locator: Year summary (Voxagon Blog) - Teardown destruction and physics
game_examples.relevance: Demonstrates the worst case for broadphase: destruction events create dense bursts of bodies rather than a steady-state distribution.
game_examples.non_transferable: Teardown's voxel representation makes its body distribution unlike a mesh-based game; the absolute counts are not transferable.

game_examples.fact: A shipped title with a very small install footprint and fast startup, showing the low end of the build-size and cold-start range.
game_examples.locator: Game article / technical reference: distribution size and startup
game_examples.relevance: Anchors the low end of the build-size and startup budget range with a real, widely distributed shipping product.
game_examples.non_transferable: Minecraft's asset footprint is dominated by procedural content and simple textures; a photoreal title cannot reach comparable install sizes regardless of pipeline quality.

game_examples.fact: A shipped title with a very large install footprint, representing the high end of the same range.
game_examples.locator: Cyberpunk 2077: Technology Preview of Path Tracing - asset and streaming scale
game_examples.relevance: Anchors the high end of the build-size range, giving the budget model a real observed spread rather than an assumption.
game_examples.non_transferable: Install size here reflects a specific content scope and audio localisation set; it is an anchor point, not a target.

game_examples.fact: A hero shooter whose abilities require separate collision queries for hitscan, projectiles, area effects, movement and line-of-sight, each with different targets.
game_examples.locator: 'Overwatch' Gameplay Architecture and Netcode (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: Shows why a collision layer matrix is a gameplay requirement and not an optimisation: different systems must see different subsets of the world.
game_examples.non_transferable: The talk does not publish the layer table, so this evidences the requirement, not a particular matrix design.

game_examples.fact: Destructible environments combined with ballistic penetration mean the same geometry must answer different queries for bullets, movement and destruction propagation.
game_examples.locator: The Art of Destruction in Rainbow Six: Siege (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example where destruction forces the collision configuration to distinguish between structural, ballistic and navigational queries.
game_examples.non_transferable: RealBlast is a bespoke destruction system; its query categories do not generalise to an engine without destructible geometry.

game_examples.fact: A live game updated very frequently, so the cost of shipping a full client for every change is unacceptable and chunked, differential updates are required.
game_examples.locator: Drop into the Next Generation of Fortnite - content delivery and update cadence
game_examples.relevance: Establishes the operating condition that makes differential patching mandatory: high update frequency at very large player counts.
game_examples.non_transferable: Epic controls both the client and the CDN; a small team's patch economics differ and are not described by this source.

game_examples.fact: A competitive title receiving frequent, small client updates where download size directly affects how quickly the player base can join a match.
game_examples.locator: Counter-Strike 2 official feature page / update delivery
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped example of frequent small-patch delivery, from a different studio and genre.
game_examples.non_transferable: No patch-size or delta-ratio figures are published, so this does not quantify patch efficiency.

game_examples.fact: The Windows port of a title built around instantaneous world transitions, delivered on PC with an SSD-oriented streaming path.
game_examples.locator: Game article: PC port technology section
game_examples.relevance: Shows the design pattern that motivates the API - transitions that assume very high storage throughput - validated in a shipped PC release.
game_examples.non_transferable: The specific IO API used by the port is not documented in this source; this evidences the pattern, not the API call.

game_examples.fact: Soft-body vehicle simulation whose stability depends on a fixed, small integration step; variable steps would change suspension and deformation behaviour.
game_examples.locator: Soft-body Physics - BeamNG.drive
game_examples.relevance: A shipped case where the fixed step is a correctness requirement for the simulation, not a performance choice.
game_examples.non_transferable: BeamNG runs a far heavier solver than a typical action game; its step size is not a usable default elsewhere.

game_examples.fact: A bullet-hell shooter with extremely dense particle effects, where the number of simultaneous emitters makes per-frame simulation of every effect unaffordable.
game_examples.locator: Visual Effects Summit: Can We Do It without Particles? - Returnal VFX
game_examples.relevance: Shows the pressure that makes baked/flipbook effects attractive: emitter density in a 60 fps action game.
game_examples.non_transferable: The talk covers Housemarque's own VFX pipeline; it does not state which effects are flipbooks versus simulated.

game_examples.fact: Hand-drawn, frame-by-frame animation throughout, i.e. a shipped game whose entire visual language is pre-baked frame sequences rather than runtime simulation.
game_examples.locator: Cuphead - A Game | Made with Unity (Unity case study)
game_examples.relevance: An extreme shipped example of the flipbook principle applied at game-wide scale.
game_examples.non_transferable: Cuphead's animation is authored art, not simulated VFX baked to textures; the pipeline constraints are completely different.

game_examples.fact: A linear, lighting-driven shooter with large interior/exterior spaces and both baked and ray-traced lighting paths.
game_examples.locator: Global Illumination in Metro Exodus: A Deep Dive (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example of a team investing in GI authoring where the baked path remains necessary for platforms without RT hardware.
game_examples.non_transferable: 4A's lighting solution is bespoke and tied to its linear level structure; it does not transfer to open-world streaming.

game_examples.fact: A shipped UE5 title with large, detailed interiors and heavy lighting, exercising the engine's lighting build pipeline on retail content.
game_examples.locator: Lords of the Fallen is a stunning UE5 showcase (technical coverage)
game_examples.relevance: Shows a licensed-engine team delivering a shipping lighting build on UE5.
game_examples.non_transferable: The source does not state which bake backend or how long the bake takes, so no build-time figure can be derived.

game_examples.fact: Planetary-scale rendering where an entire planet must be representable from orbit down to surface detail, forcing many levels of distance-based reduction.
game_examples.locator: Continuous World Generation in 'No Man's Sky' (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: Extreme-range LOD: the depth of the LOD hierarchy is dictated by planetary scale rather than by art direction.
game_examples.non_transferable: Procedural planets generate LODs differently from authored meshes; the HLOD tooling is not transferable.

game_examples.fact: A large open world with dense vegetation and long view distances, requiring distant objects to be merged and simplified to stay within the draw budget.
game_examples.locator: Streaming the World of Horizon Zero Dawn (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped open-world example where HLOD is what makes long draw distances affordable.
game_examples.non_transferable: Decima's streaming and LOD pipeline is bespoke; the具体实现 is not documented in enough detail to copy.

game_examples.fact: Lighting-driven gameplay with many practical light sources in large spaces, making light range and attenuation a direct runtime cost.
game_examples.locator: Global Illumination in Metro Exodus: A Deep Dive (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped case where the number and range of lights is a primary performance lever rather than an incidental setting.
game_examples.non_transferable: No per-light cost figures are published; the example establishes the cost driver, not its magnitude.

game_examples.fact: A horror title whose reading of space depends on practical lights and shadows, so light count and range are gameplay-critical and must be budgeted.
game_examples.locator: How Northlight makes Alan Wake 2 shine (Remedy technology article)
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped example from a different studio where light attenuation is central to both look and cost.
game_examples.non_transferable: Northlight's lighting model is bespoke; ranges and counts do not transfer.

game_examples.fact: A 2D title with painted, pre-lit backgrounds, i.e. lighting resolved at authoring time rather than at runtime.
game_examples.locator: Rayman Legends: The Design Process (UbiArt pipeline)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped 2D example of baked lighting as the primary lighting solution.
game_examples.non_transferable: UbiArt's baked lighting is art-directed painting, not a physical bake; it does not generalise to dynamically lit 2D scenes.

game_examples.fact: A 2D Unity title whose hand-drawn assets bake all shading into the artwork.
game_examples.locator: Cuphead - A Game | Made with Unity (Unity case study)
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped 2D example, from a different studio and pipeline.
game_examples.non_transferable: No runtime lighting at all; this is the degenerate case of a 2D lightmap bake.

game_examples.fact: Large linear levels with baked lighting, requiring surface UV atlasing across a wide area.
game_examples.locator: Global Illumination in Metro Exodus: A Deep Dive (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: Shows atlas-scale baking in shipped, large-scale levels rather than in a demo scene.
game_examples.non_transferable: The atlas packing strategy and resolution are not published.

game_examples.fact: A shipped UE5 title with large, highly detailed environments that must be lit within console and PC memory limits.
game_examples.locator: Black Myth: Wukong - the PC tech review
game_examples.relevance: A recent shipped example of a licensed-engine team solving lighting at retail scale.
game_examples.non_transferable: The review does not document the lightmap atlas configuration, so no bake setting can be inferred.

game_examples.fact: A streaming open world in which lighting data must be paged in with the terrain, making lightmap size a streaming-bandwidth concern.
game_examples.locator: Streaming the World of Horizon Zero Dawn (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: Establishes the coupling that forces lightmap compression: lighting data competes for streaming budget with geometry and textures.
game_examples.non_transferable: Decima's streaming format is proprietary; compression ratios are not published.

game_examples.fact: A shipped title combining baked lighting with a separately shipped ray-traced path, so both lighting representations coexist in the same build.
game_examples.locator: Global Illumination in Metro Exodus: A Deep Dive (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: Shows a project carrying two lighting solutions, which increases the pressure on lightmap memory.
game_examples.non_transferable: No memory or compression figures are published for either path.

game_examples.fact: Character fidelity is a primary deliverable, requiring high-detail source sculpts reduced to a shippable real-time mesh.
game_examples.locator: The making of Senua's Saga: Hellblade II (technical coverage)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example of a cinematic-fidelity character pipeline delivered by a mid-sized team.
game_examples.non_transferable: Ninja Theory used photogrammetry and bespoke tooling; the pipeline cost is not transferable and no mesh budgets are published.

game_examples.fact: Highly detailed character and environment assets delivered on UE5 at retail quality.
game_examples.locator: Black Myth: Wukong - the PC tech review
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped example of high-density assets requiring normal-map based reduction.
game_examples.non_transferable: The review does not describe the baking pipeline; the example demonstrates the requirement, not the method.

game_examples.fact: Vehicles and debris that come to rest must stop consuming solver time, otherwise a large scene of parked vehicles remains permanently expensive.
game_examples.locator: Soft-body Physics - BeamNG.drive
game_examples.relevance: A shipped simulation title where sleeping/deactivation is a hard requirement for scene scale.
game_examples.non_transferable: Sleeping thresholds here interact with a soft-body solver; tuning for rigid bodies would differ.

game_examples.fact: After a destruction event the resulting debris must settle and stop simulating, or the scene cost never returns to baseline.
game_examples.locator: Year summary (Voxagon Blog) - Teardown destruction and physics
game_examples.relevance: Demonstrates deactivation as the mechanism that restores the frame budget after a burst.
game_examples.non_transferable: Voxel debris has different settling behaviour from rigid-body meshes; the parameters do not transfer.

game_examples.fact: A fully ray-traced remaster in which reflections are resolved globally rather than by re-rendering a mirrored view per surface.
game_examples.locator: Quake II RTX: Re-Engineering a Classic (SIGGRAPH/GDC presentation)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped contrast case: the same reflection requirement met by a completely different technique, which is what a planar-reflection budget has to be weighed against.
game_examples.non_transferable: Q2VKPT is a research-grade renderer requiring RTX hardware; it is not a substitute for a planar reflection path on mid-range GPUs.

game_examples.fact: A shipped puzzle game built entirely around recursive portal rendering, where each visible portal requires re-rendering part of the scene.
game_examples.locator: Game article: portal gameplay and rendering sections
game_examples.relevance: The canonical shipped example of portals as a core rendering cost rather than as an effect.
game_examples.non_transferable: Source's portal rendering is integrated into the engine's vis/rendering pipeline; a render-target-based approach in a modern engine has a different cost profile.

game_examples.fact: A lighting-heavy title where contact darkening carries material separation in interiors.
game_examples.locator: Exploring Ray Traced Future in Metro Exodus (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example of contact-shadow quality being a visible, budgeted lighting feature.
game_examples.non_transferable: The source contrasts RT and raster techniques; it does not publish a per-effect cost.

game_examples.fact: Dark, practical-lit scenes where contact shadows are essential to grounding objects.
game_examples.locator: How Northlight makes Alan Wake 2 shine (Remedy technology article)
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped example from a different studio, in a genre where shadow contact is narratively important.
game_examples.non_transferable: Northlight's shadow pipeline is bespoke; no cost figure is published.

game_examples.fact: Light shafts are used as a core visual motif in dark forest and interior scenes.
game_examples.locator: How Northlight makes Alan Wake 2 shine (Remedy technology article)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example where volumetric light scattering is a headline visual feature rather than an optional post effect.
game_examples.non_transferable: Remedy's volumetric implementation is bespoke and its cost is not published.

game_examples.fact: Dense atmospheric particle and light-shaft effects layered on top of heavy combat VFX.
game_examples.locator: Visual Effects Summit: Can We Do It without Particles? - Returnal VFX
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped example, showing volumetric effects competing for budget with dense gameplay VFX.
game_examples.non_transferable: The talk does not separate the cost of light shafts from other VFX.

game_examples.fact: Discrete, player-managed worlds saved as separate save slots, i.e. the classic snapshot-per-slot model.
game_examples.locator: Chunk format / world save layout
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example of slot-based saves coexisting with incremental per-region writes.
game_examples.non_transferable: Minecraft's slot model has no progression state to reconcile; a narrative game's save schema is far more constrained.

game_examples.fact: Multiple saved expeditions persisted alongside a shared generated universe.
game_examples.locator: Continuous World Generation in 'No Man's Sky' (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped example of slot-based persistence under a very large world state.
game_examples.non_transferable: Save schema details are not published; the example shows the pattern, not the implementation.

game_examples.fact: A 2D title with very large numbers of animated sprites on screen, where per-sprite draw calls would dominate the frame.
game_examples.locator: Rayman Legends: The Design Process (UbiArt pipeline)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped 2D example where sprite batching is a precondition for the target frame rate.
game_examples.non_transferable: UbiArt's batching is built into a bespoke 2D engine; a general-purpose engine's 2D batcher behaves differently.

game_examples.fact: Hand-drawn frame animation used for characters, projectiles and effects alike, so effects are sprite frames rather than simulated particles.
game_examples.locator: Cuphead - A Game | Made with Unity (Unity case study)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example of particle-like effects delivered entirely from sprite frame atlases.
game_examples.non_transferable: This is authored art rather than a particle system; it does not evidence runtime particle batching behaviour.

game_examples.fact: Very high on-screen sprite counts including effect frames, requiring atlased sources.
game_examples.locator: Rayman Legends: The Design Process (UbiArt pipeline)
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped 2D example from a different studio and engine.
game_examples.non_transferable: Same limitation: bespoke 2D pipeline, no published batching figures.

game_examples.fact: Full-screen hand-drawn animation frames, where uncompressed sprite sheets would dominate the build and memory budget.
game_examples.locator: Rayman Legends: The Design Process (UbiArt pipeline)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped case where sprite sheet size is a primary memory driver, which is the condition that makes sheet compression a budget item.
game_examples.non_transferable: Compression settings are not published and UbiArt's format is proprietary.

game_examples.fact: A shipped Unity 2D title whose hand-drawn pipeline depends on keeping draw calls low across thousands of frames of artwork.
game_examples.locator: Cuphead - A Game | Made with Unity (Unity case study)
game_examples.relevance: Shows draw-call discipline as a shipping requirement in Unity specifically, which is the problem SRP Batcher addresses.
game_examples.non_transferable: IMPORTANT: Cuphead predates URP/SRP Batcher, so it evidences the requirement (draw-call pressure in Unity) but NOT the SRP Batcher feature. It is recorded at partial match level for that reason.

game_examples.fact: The world is divided into fixed-size chunks that are loaded and unloaded around the player, which is the canonical tile/world chunk streaming model.
game_examples.locator: Chunk format / chunk loading and simulation distance
game_examples.relevance: A shipped, extremely widely deployed example of chunk-granular world streaming.
game_examples.non_transferable: Minecraft chunks are voxel blocks with simple schemas; a tilemap with per-layer metadata has different streaming costs.

game_examples.fact: Only chunks within simulation and render distance are processed, so per-chunk culling is what bounds both simulation and rendering cost.
game_examples.locator: Simulation distance / chunk loading behaviour
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example of distance-based culling bounding work at chunk granularity.
game_examples.non_transferable: Minecraft's culling is per 16x16 chunk; a 2D tilemap's layer culling is a different axis.

game_examples.fact: A large open world with many vehicles, aircraft and physics props, where only nearby vehicles can be fully simulated.
game_examples.locator: Vehicle Physics and Tire Dynamics in 'Just Cause 4' (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped open-world example where vehicle simulation detail must degrade with distance and relevance.
game_examples.non_transferable: The talk covers full-detail vehicle physics, not the LOD policy; the degradation strategy is not documented.

game_examples.fact: A shipped game whose world is a voxel grid, i.e. the scene representation that voxel-based GI techniques operate on directly.
game_examples.locator: Year summary (Voxagon Blog) - Teardown voxel world and lighting
game_examples.relevance: Demonstrates a shipped voxel world representation, which is the precondition for voxel cone tracing rather than an implementation of it.
game_examples.non_transferable: Teardown does not implement voxel cone tracing; this evidences the data representation, not the algorithm.

game_examples.fact: A shipped title with a layered post-processing stack (volumetrics, depth of field, gradation) applied selectively per scene rather than uniformly.
game_examples.locator: How Northlight makes Alan Wake 2 shine (Remedy technology article)
game_examples.relevance: Shows selective post-effect application as a shipped, art-directed practice.
game_examples.non_transferable: Northlight's stack is bespoke and no per-effect cost breakdown is published.

game_examples.fact: A shipped open-city title with an extensive, tiered post-processing stack that scales by quality preset.
game_examples.locator: Path Tracing & Overdrive Mode - requirements and post stack
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped example where post effects are budgeted and tiered rather than fixed.
game_examples.non_transferable: REDengine's stack and its presets are engine-specific; costs are not published.

game_examples.fact: A shipped title that performs shader/state pre-compilation before gameplay specifically to avoid hitching during play.
game_examples.locator: Rendering the Hellscape of Doom Eternal (SIGGRAPH Advances)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example of pre-caching as a load-time step taken deliberately to remove runtime stalls.
game_examples.non_transferable: id Tech 7 is a bespoke engine with a small, controlled shader set; the warm-up cost in a licensed engine with combinatorial variants is far larger.

game_examples.fact: A shipped UE5 title whose first-launch shader compilation is a visible, widely reported part of the PC experience.
game_examples.locator: Black Myth: Wukong - the PC tech review
game_examples.relevance: The counter-example: shows what happens when PSO/shader warm-up is incomplete, which is why pre-caching is a planned task rather than an optimisation.
game_examples.non_transferable: No measured compilation time is published here; the example establishes the risk, not its magnitude.

game_examples.fact: A 2D platformer with per-layer lighting and shadowing, where the number of shadow casters has to be bounded by design.
game_examples.locator: Rayman Legends: The Design Process (UbiArt pipeline)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped 2D example where shadow-caster count is an authored limit, not an engine default.
game_examples.non_transferable: UbiArt's 2D lighting is bespoke; the numeric limits are not published.

game_examples.fact: A 2D Unity title where all shading is authored, i.e. the degenerate case of a zero-cost 2D shadow setup.
game_examples.locator: Cuphead - A Game | Made with Unity (Unity case study)
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped 2D example anchoring the low end of the 2D shadow budget range.
game_examples.non_transferable: No runtime shadow casting at all; this bounds the range but does not model a dynamic 2D shadow system.

game_examples.fact: Large static levels where shadowing for static geometry can be resolved once rather than every frame.
game_examples.locator: Global Illumination in Metro Exodus: A Deep Dive (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: A shipped example of static/dynamic shadow separation as a budget strategy.
game_examples.non_transferable: The caching mechanism and its memory cost are not published.

game_examples.fact: A streaming open world with a time-of-day cycle, i.e. the hard case where static shadow caching competes with moving light.
game_examples.locator: Streaming the World of Horizon Zero Dawn (GDC)
game_examples.relevance: Second shipped example showing the constraint that limits static shadow caching: dynamic sun angle and streamed world state.
game_examples.non_transferable: Decima's shadow caching is proprietary; no figures are published.

claims.statement: No shipped commercial title was located that uses neural texture compression. The located evidence covers the research/SDK stage only, so no game example is asserted here.
claims.locator: n/a - declared absence, no source supports a game example
claims.context: Declared honestly under the study rule that absence of a source is not evidence of adoption.

claims.statement: No shipped commercial title was located that implements a temporal radiance cache. It is a research-stage technique; asserting a game example would be fabrication.
claims.locator: n/a - declared absence, no source supports a game example
claims.context: Declared honestly under the study rule that absence of a source is not evidence of adoption.
